The kernel exists and is wired (crates/shadow-model/src/cpu_expert_avx512.rs, call sites in cpu_expert.rs row_dot/quantize) but the ARCHITECTURE PIECES are what must be built: the no-join submission path and the copy-set exclusion.
what_to_build: 1. CPU computes cache-miss experts straight from the mmap'd file (page cache -> CPU registers = ONE DRAM read), replacing the path where bytes cross DRAM 3-4 times. The kernel already exists and is fast enough (0.088-0.136 ms/expert, 17-21 GB/s on 14 threads, measured on this machine). DO NOT optimize the kernel.
2. CPU writes each expert's activation row into the pinned region; the existing copy completion mechanism brings that small row up. NO host join - the previous three attempts' fatal flaw.
3. Those experts are EXCLUDED from the big-weight copy set; only the ~3 KB output row is copied.
4. CPU job submitted as soon as the router's tops are known (the 'pre' group's output), so CPU time hides under the GPU's resident-expert work.

5. Gate behind an env var (SHADOW_AVALON=1 style); baseline (gate off) stays default until measured. The two defensive edits already landed in readpool.rs submit_locked (assert! -> checked error return) - keep them, they are green.

6. The three previous failed attempts computed FROM THE PINNED BYTES (no DRAM saving) and the host waited for pool completion before combine (the join). GPU-wait reduction worked exactly as predicted (58 -> 46 -> 39 ms/pass) but the CPU time moved into the host join and the pass stayed 104 ms. Fix exactly those two structural problems.

net_dram_math_per_expert_moved_to_cpu: old GPU path: 3 big DRAM passes (4.5 MB); new CPU path: 1 big read (1.5 MB) + 2 small passes for the 3 KB output row. ~3x traffic reduction for bytes moved to the CPU.
